explanation: One of the twelve disciples who witnessed Jesus' resurrection and wrote this gospel to strengthen faith that Jesus is the Messiah, God's Son.
The event where Jesus returned from the dead with a physical body three days after his crucifixion, confirming his divine nature.
The place where Jesus' body was laid to rest in a stone cave before he rose again.
Covered the entrance to the tomb and symbolizes the power of death that Jesus overcame by rolling it away.
Mary from Magdala, the first person to see the risen Jesus and was sent to tell the disciples the news.
Describes the state of the tomb after the stone was removed; the body was missing because Jesus had risen.
The angel's help or invitation to observe the empty tomb as proof of the resurrection.
The term used by the disciples and Mary to describe the female followers who first came to the tomb early on Sunday morning.
The physical end of life that Jesus overcame, giving hope of eternal life for all believers.
The title Jesus gave himself in John 14:6; he is the source of both present and eternal life through his resurrection.
